Subject: Post-demo: Data handling & marketplace sharing questions

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo today. Great product fit for our beta use cases. Per our ask, I captured a short list of follow-ups so our security and product teams can qualify: 

1) PII surface: which fields from user events do you consider PII? Please confirm whether email and device identifiers are treated as PII in your logs.
2) Retention: what are default retention windows for raw request logs vs aggregated telemetry? Can we set a custom 90- or 180-day retention for our account?
3) Third-party telemetry/sharing: which subprocessors receive event-level telemetry (analytics, observability, marketplace integrations)? Please list vendor names and their purpose.
4) Data residency: do you have controls to guarantee that customer telemetry is stored only in US regions? Any EU/APAC options?
5) Logging controls: can you redact or hash user identifiers before sending to downstream analytics vendors?

Attachments: I’m including a short Redwood checklist (see attached) — helps us map your answers to our DPA/Security review.

Next steps we propose: if your security team can return the completed questionnaire and a subprocessor list by EOD Friday, we’ll run a quick legal/infra qual and aim to move to a short POC. Also happy to do a 30-min security call if helpful.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@marketflow.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Data handling & marketplace sharing questions

Hi Kimberly — appreciate the clear recap. Answers below and I attached our completed security questionnaire. Happy to jump on a call tomorrow to walk through details.

1) PII surface: Our primary event schema includes user_id (internal id), email (optional), device_id, ip_address, page_url, and event_name. We classify email and ip_address as PII. We already support masking email on ingest.

2) Retention: Default raw event retention is 365 days. Aggregates (rolled-up metrics) are retained for 2 years. We can offer a custom retention policy for enterprise customers; common options are 90/180/365 days.

3) Third-party telemetry/sharing: We use the following subprocessors: Segment (analytics routing), Amplitude (product analytics), and Datadog (observability/alerts). Marketplace integrations (third-party connectors in our app store) may optionally pull anonymized event-level telemetry for connector verification — this is opt-in per customer. We attached the vendor list in the questionnaire.

4) Data residency: We run primary storage in AWS us-west-2 for US accounts. EU and APAC regions are available but require a region flag during onboarding. We can scope your account to US-only.

5) Logging controls: Yes — we support server-side hashing of email and device_id at ingest, and can redact ip_address. We can also provide a filter to prevent forwarding event payloads to specific vendors (e.g., block Segment forwarding for event_type=checkout).

Attached: marketflow-security-questionnaire.xlsx

Let us know if you want a short technical discussion.

Best,
Alex Turner
Solutions Engineer, Marketflow Inc.
alex.turner@marketflow.com

Kim — quick read. Surface-level thoughts: Segment as a routing layer is common but it is a telemetry vector we should be careful about — if they forward PII to Segment we need a contract clause and evidence of processing controls. Amplitude and Datadog are fine so long as they only receive pseudonymized ids.

On retention, 90 days for raw events + 365 for aggregates seems like an acceptable compromise for a POC. Require them to hash emails at ingest and provide a technical attestation that hashing happens in US region before any forwarding.

If you ask them for an attestation + a signed subprocessor list, we can move forward to a POC. Also add a clause preventing any marketplace connector from pulling event-level PII without explicit written consent.

-rishi
Head of Security Architecture (incoming)

Adding a few practical asks we should make to Marketflow in the next message: 
- Signed subprocessor list (including contract references) and SOC2 report or equivalent for Segment/Amplitude/Datadog.
- 90-day raw retention option + written confirmation of per-account region scoping (us-west-2).
- Technical proof: a short runbook or diagram showing where hashing/redaction occurs (pre-forwarding).
- Contract language: no marketplace connector may pull event-level PII without our opt-in; require DPA amendment for any connector that needs event-level data.

If Marketflow can confirm the above, I support moving to a limited internal POC. I’ll attach our checklist (redwood-telemetry-checklist-v1.pdf) with the ask list and can help run the security call.
